title: Initial token stall caused by priority eviction across multi-model serving
creator: Sanjay Rao
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported a sharp increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and a sustained drop in tokens/sec for short-context chat requests after the runtime kernel-scheduler heuristic change deployed on 2026-03-08. Impact spanned small-context assistant prompts (<=128 tokens), low-batch traffic, and multiplexed routes. Several enterprise customers filed escalations with production traces showing 600-1,200ms additional TTFT and 30-50% TPS regression for affected variants.

Why this ticket: This issue needs an emergency coordinated fix (rollback + targeted patch), routing mitigations for enterprise customers currently impacted, and longer-term scheduler + cache hardening to avoid recurrence. The document below captures timeline, repro, immediate mitigations, and post-incident follow-ups.
timeline:
2026-03-08 02:10 UTC - Deploy of scheduler heuristic v4 which changed model-stride prediction and eviction windows.
2026-03-08 09:35 UTC - Pager alerts: 3 customer-reported TTFT spikes across hosted region us-west2.
2026-03-08 11:00 UTC - Engineering on-call begins triage; observed increased CPU steal on worker pods handling multiplexed short-context requests.
2026-03-08 13:20 UTC - Repro in staging: small-context chat jobs show 700ms TTFT increase when heuristic marks short requests as low-priority and evicts their KV/prefix entries aggressively.
2026-03-08 15:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: route critical customers to dedicated pools and enable "preserve-short-context-cache" flag in hosted for high-tier customers.
2026-03-09 03:40 UTC - Rollback of scheduler heuristic v4 to v3 across hosted region us-west2 completed; preliminary TTFT improvement confirmed.
2026-03-09 10:25 UTC - Patch PR opened to add priority-aware cache pinning and backpressure isolation for multiplex queues.
2026-03-11 08:00 UTC - Ongoing: private/on-prem update playbook drafted; coordinated customer communications sent.
root_cause: A change to the kernel-level scheduling heuristic introduced an aggressive priority eviction policy for short-context requests: the stride-based prediction misclassified many short interactive requests as "low throughput candidates" leading to premature KV/prefix cache eviction and demotion in the multiplexer queue. This caused recomputation of KV caches, extra kernel launches, and serialization that amplified TTFT and reduced tokens/sec for affected traffic patterns. The heuristic interacted poorly with QUIC connection reuse and our KV cache retention thresholds, producing a systemic regression across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments that applied the same runtime binary.
mitigation_steps: Immediate rollback of scheduler heuristic v4 to v3 in affected hosted and dedicated regions (done for us-west2, in-progress for eu-west1)
Enabled preserve-short-context-cache flag for high-tier hosted customers to avoid cache eviction while we patch the scheduler
Rerouted three enterprise customers with escalations to dedicated pools with conservative cache retention settings (manual routing rules applied)
Customer communications: incident bulletin and workaround instructions published to affected customers and success teams
Created temporary autoscaling cap to throttle low-priority background workloads on nodes serving multiplexed short-context traffic
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime v1.20 with scheduler heuristic v4 to staging OR reproduce using the runtime image used in production on a cluster with multiplexing enabled
Send 1000 short-context (<=128 tokens) chat requests across 100 concurrent connections simulating PLG traffic; observe median TTFT baseline vs with heuristic enabled
Capture KV cache hit/miss rates and multiplexer queue latency; reproduce the ~700ms TTFT increase and 30-50% TPS regression
Toggle preserve-short-context-cache flag to verify TTFT recovery in same environment
rollout_plan: Short term (now -> 72h): audit remaining deployments for v4 usage and rollback where necessary; keep preserve-short-context-cache enabled for impacted customers; complete dedicated-pool routing for escalations

Medium term (72h -> 14d): land PR that pins short-context requests in KV/prefix cache and adjusts eviction windows based on per-tenant traffic patterns; add multiplexer queue isolation when cache miss spike detected

Long term (14d -> 90d): rework stride predictor to include connection+prompt shape telemetry, add canary tests that include short-context chat traffic profiles, and add synthetic SLOs for TTFT across model families
follow_ups: PR-5421: priority-aware cache pinning (owner: @evelynchen) - target merge by 2026-03-13
ENG-65400: add canary tests for short-context TTFT across all model variants
DOC-179: private deployment playbook for emergency scheduler rollback (owner: SRE)
Monitoring: create a dedicated TTFT SLI and dashboard per-customer; add alert when 95th percentile TTFT for <=128 token requests increases >200ms
